beats.narration: If you stopped sleeping, after just one day, tiny parts of your brain would start falling asleep... while you're still awake.

shots.scene_description: Man in bed at night, eyes wide open, clock showing hour 24
Brain with patches dimming and Zs floating out

beats.narration: These are called microsleeps. For a few seconds, your brain simply switches off, and you don't even notice.

shots.scene_description: Man at a desk, eyes drooping shut then snapping open
Brain power switch flicking OFF for 3 seconds

beats.narration: After twenty-four hours awake, your reaction time is about as bad as someone who's legally drunk.

shots.scene_description: Reaction-time bar growing, = DRUNK stamp
Man swaying with stars circling his head

beats.narration: That's because while you sleep, your brain runs a cleaning system that washes away the waste built up during the day. Skip sleep, and the trash piles up.

shots.scene_description: Brain washed by blue fluid sweeping waste away
Brain with trash dots piling up

beats.narration: Your body gets confused too. The hormone that makes you hungry goes up, and the one that tells you you're full goes down. So you crave junk food.

shots.scene_description: Two hormone meters: HUNGER up, FULL down
Junk food floating toward the man

beats.narration: Your immune system gets weaker, which makes it easier to catch a cold.

shots.scene_description: Immune shield cracking as germs approach
Man with a red nose, ACHOO

beats.narration: By day three, many people start seeing things that aren't there: walls that seem to move, and shapes in the corner of their eye.

shots.scene_description: Bedroom walls wobbling, DAY 3
Shadowy shapes in the corner, giant eye

beats.narration: But here's the crazy part. In 1964, a seventeen-year-old named Randy Gardner stayed awake for eleven whole days.

shots.scene_description: Calendar 1964 with a 17-year-old
Day counter rolling to DAY 11

beats.narration: By the end, he struggled to remember things and even hallucinated. It became so risky that Guinness World Records stopped accepting attempts.

shots.scene_description: Confused teen with question marks
Record book with red X

beats.narration: So tonight, put the phone down. Sleep isn't wasted time... it's when your brain repairs itself.

shots.scene_description: Phone screen switching off on a nightstand
Man sleeping peacefully, brain in REPAIR MODE
